title: implicit-peer-grouping: adaptive NCCL concurrency + KV-cache affinity for unbalanced tensor-parallel jobs
author: Ana Sato
description:
Motivation: Production TP workloads often have heterogeneous layer split sizes and uneven per-rank compute, which amplifies NCCL tail latency and leads to stalled KV-cache prefetch pipelines. This PR introduces an implicit peer-grouping heuristic plus adaptive NCCL-concurrency controls and KV-cache affinity to reduce cross-rank variance and improve end-to-end throughput.

Summary of changes: single continuous change that adds (1) a lightweight runtime pass that forms implicit peer groups for collective launches when layer shapes indicate skewed tensor slices; (2) a dynamic NCCL concurrency limiter that adjusts concurrent collective in-flight windows based on observed micro-latency, with conservative fallback to ring mode on high variance; (3) a KV-cache affinity allocator that prefetches and pins frequently-accessed KV shards to the GPU streams most likely to consume them, reducing host-device sync stalls; (4) a new scheduling metric (rank-skew-score) exposed in tracing and metrics to drive autoscaling decisions.

Benchmarks: using the perf-lab harness and the multi-node 8xA100 cluster we saw: median tail token latency reduced by 18-26% on mismatched-slice synthetic workloads, aggregate throughput improvement of 11% on a 1.4B model with uneven layer slice distribution, and steady-state token/sec improvement of 6% on a real-world customer request trace used under SUP-3187. Microbenchmarks for collective overlap show a 30% reduction in wasted idle time between kernel launches in high-skew scenarios.

Compatibility and safety: default behavior is opt-in via new runtime flag `tp_implicit_peer_grouping=true`. When disabled, all existing behavior is preserved. The NCCL concurrency controller respects user-specified concurrency ceilings and falls back to previous heuristics on any unexpected mpi/nccl failures. The KV-cache allocator only uses memory already reserved for KV shards and does not change shard sizes.

Testing: unit tests for peer-group formation and KV affinity allocator added; integration benchmark harness updated with a new `tp-skewed-slices` job; e2e test on a 4-node staging cluster exercised fallback paths and validated no correctness regressions. CI: initial runs had a flaky test in bench harness which was hardened; final CI status green.

Related: follows work in ENG-4921 (scheduling heuristics) and complements PRs that adjusted NCCL stream prioritization in earlier patches. Linear tickets ENG-5014 tracks adding the metric to the console and alerting rules.

Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness of peer-group boundaries on line 147 of src/runtime/tp/implicit_peer_group.cpp and the concurrency limiter's state machine in src/runtime/comm/nccl_concurrency_controller.cpp. The KV affinity allocator is intentionally conservative; look for opportunities to reduce copy overhead in the affinity placement heuristic.

review_thread: Marcus Lee: Looks good overall. Can you justify the default thresholds? Suggest exposing them as runtime knobs.
Ana Sato (author): Added flags `tp_peer_group_variance_threshold` and `tp_concurrency_ceiling` with sensible defaults; documented in docs/perf/nccl-implicit-groups.md.
Priya Nair: KV affinity is conservative which is good. Did you measure cases where this increases PCIe pressure?

Ana Sato (author): Measured PCIe pressure on the 8xA100 cluster; no significant increase since allocator pins only within already-reserved KV pages. Added microbenchmark results to the PR description.

Jonah Kim: a couple nits in the scheduler metrics naming and one flaky test seen in CI.
Requested change: rename `rank_skew` -> `rank_skew_score` and add stabilization loop to tests.
Ana Sato (author): Renamed metric, added stabilization wait in test harness, and reran CI; green now.
release_notes: Reduce TP tail latency for skewed-slice workloads by forming implicit peer groups, adding an adaptive NCCL concurrency controller, and introducing KV-cache affinity. Opt-in via runtime flag `tp_implicit_peer_grouping`.
notes: Operational: enable with caution for customers on dedicated clusters; recommend pilot for high-skew models.
Follow-up: expose metric in Console (ENG-5014) and add a canary rollout rule to gradually enable on Dedicated.
Rollback plan: toggle runtime flag to false and optionally set `tp_concurrency_ceiling=1` to revert to prior behavior.
